title.narrative: Teach for Future: the future of Zubair is in my classroom today

description.narrative:
The crises that Iraq has faced in the past few decades have had a negative impact on its learning environment and the provision of inclusive and equitable quality education for all. To mitigate these negative impacts, UNESCO is collaborating and supporting the government as well as non-governmental organizations in Iraq through technical and financial assistance to improve policy and planning, management and implementation of quality teaching and learning opportunities for all. In doing so UNESCO mobilizes from public and private partnerships.
As an important partner in the extractive industry in Iraq since 2009, Eni is committed to increasing investment towards sustainability in Iraq in the coming years and has identified the education sector as a key target for its ‘Social Intervention’ activities. Eni’s commitment to education is to be accomplished through programmes aimed at promoting and improving access to quality education in close collaboration with local communities and authorities, contributing to guaranteeing sustainable and quality education to new generations, especially in the geographical areas in which Eni operates in Iraq. Eni aims to support efforts to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all, in line with the goals and targets of Sustainable Development Goal 4, and in alignment with the priorities of Iraqi’s National Development Plan 2017-2022, Iraq Vision 2030 and the new National Education Strategy 2022-2031.
Building on a preliminary assessment conducted by Eni in 2019 that involved a selected yet significant section of the social and educational system in Al Zubair, Eni has envisaged - along with the Directorate of Education of Basra - a tailored “Teach for Future” project to be implemented in the Al Zubair district of Basra Governorate that directly responds to the teaching and learning needs of the children, teachers, parents and school management community and district of 131 primary schools in the Al Zubair district. “Teach for Future” will be a tailored project that will focus on three interlinked components:
i. Improved learning environment: improvement of infrastructures (including new constructions) and basic services in Al Zubair; ii. Teaching and learning practices: - teaching and learning tools developed and teachers’ capacities improved for the effective implementation of a child/learner centred approach to quality teaching and learning; - capacity enhancement for principals and DoE representatives to promote and implement innovative school management strategies and practices. iii. Pro-active role of communities, families and local authorities: empowerment of families and communities to practice child protection and play a proactive role in advancing quality education and learning for their children.
The project will specifically focus on implementing the in-class learning environment under the first component and second and third components stated above.
The physical aspects (construction and rehabilitation) of the first component is already under implementation by Eni Iraq BV. Since 2020, six school have been renovated in Basra Governorate reaching about 5.200 students, while a New High School for 700 female students is currently under construction in Zubair.
